env.name: Environment & lighting
env.scope: Skyline, atmosphere, fog, tone mapping, bloom, SSAO, colour grade

issues.text: At the default tactical camera, Arad is still an octagon of equal square blocks with glowing tan outlines on a blank plain. The new 'villa quarter' to the east is a perfect ellipse of red-roofed houses around a loop lane, with a straight spur in. From above it reads as a racetrack or a stadium, which is the most procedural-looking object in the frame. The west lobe is a thin Y of sheds, and the walled compounds are lone square tiles. In S6 the town is still a band of silver-white boxes, not warm windows on dark massing. Next to Age of Empires IV and CS2 overviews, this is a first-glance prototype tell.

Three of the seven canonical frames are about 60% empty flat beige plane. S1's foreground is a uniform featureless surface, with nothing between the camera and the town. In S3 the plateau to the horizon is a single flat tone with no rocks, wadis, scrub or relief. In S7 the bottom two-thirds is an even grey-brown sheet. The claimed shrubs and desert-pavement mottling are invisible at these distances. Iron Harvest and CoH3 never leave half the screen as a flat albedo, and TW:WH3 foregrounds always carry rock, relief or vegetation.

The regional roads render as blue-black tubes that look raised above the ground. In S7 the Route 31 line and the long diagonal look like cables lying on the desert. In S1 a dark navy rope curves in from the left. The town.js comment says far asphalt should read as a pale grey line, but in the shots it is the darkest value in the scene, and it is cold blue against the warm ground.

The plateau still ends in a ruler-straight horizontal line against the far ridge in S3 and S6. There is no visible drop, rift haze or cliff band, so the mid-ground layer (escarpment and Dead Sea) is missing from both frames, and the composition goes straight from flat ground to the ridge. In S6 the far ridge is a flat uniform band, and above it is a huge empty black sky.

Roofs are still flat grey slabs with a single box and a red dot, repeated across buildings. The rooftop clutter claimed to be bigger is not readable at S4 zoom. The block interiors are flat brown, and the scrub decals are square yellow-green tiles with hard edges. The battery vehicles in S3 are simple box clusters.

env.note: Critic R3: 5/10 (2 rounds without improvement; round 4 is the last before flagging). S4/S5 near 6–7; wide frames (S1, S2, S3, S6, S7) still read as generated: octagon core and racetrack villa loop, empty beige foreground, cable-like far roads, straight plateau rim.

vfx.name: VFX
vfx.scope: Launches, interceptor trails, intercepts, debris, smoke, screen shake

issues.text: In C5 (every frame, x~488 y~250 at 960) and S9 (x~815 y~435), an earlier impact column renders as a solid, hard-edged, dark rounded egg about 30x40 px with no wisps, no shear and no fire light. It is the most obvious 'sprite-looking puff / hard-edged circle' failure sign in the slice, and it sits next to the hero impact in the canonical Nevatim shot. CoH3 and WARNO distant columns are tall, tapered and translucent, sheared by wind.

C4 f00097: a nearby ballistic hot trail curls into a bright orange J-hook at the left edge. C4 f00108: the same object becomes a full-height thin vertical orange pillar with a pale column beside it and a broad warm wash over the left third of the frame. Width capping helped, but the pillar and hook remain. They read as a rendering glitch, not a meteor.

After each endo kill the lingering smoke is still an isolated, round, soft grey puff about 30-45 px across at 1600 (S5 x~1145 y~370, C4 x~683 y~225 in f00097 and f00108). They float alone, well away from the explosion, with a near-circular outline. CoH3 and WARNO post-kill smoke is torn, directional and connected to the burst.

S6 (t=222.7) still lands between kills. The store-page frame for 'Arrow 3 over the Dead Sea' shows about ten short orange streaks falling in parallel, like spent fireworks, with no star and no visible remnant smear. In C1 the same drizzle surrounds every star (f00030, f00084). Broken Arrow's exo kills leave a bright point plus a faint expanding smudge, not a shower of orange rockets.

S7 from the high tactical camera: Nevatim has one dark column about 25-30 px wide (x~990 y~240 at 1600) with a small fire base. Along the escarpment there is a row of 8-10 near-identical pale puffs, each with a bright point at its base, evenly spaced. The row reads as procedural repetition. CoH3 aftermath frames are dominated by a few big, wind-sheared columns of varied size.

In C1 and S6, the Arrow boost-phase trails still appear only as wide, very faint blue vertical bands on the right side of the sky (C1 f00030, x 650-850). They read as aurora or searchlights, not as lit missile smoke.
David's Sling trails overhead in S5/C4 are clean but thin white lines about 3-6 px wide. They lack the billowing width of the Dome launch ribbons.

vfx.note: Critic R3: 7/10 (better in absolute terms; 1 round without a higher score). Critic: fixing the dark 'egg' columns, near-camera re-entry pillars and the between-kills S6 frame makes 8 plausible. Round 4 building.

hud.name: HUD & UX
hud.scope: Alert countdown, objectives, shelter routing — cinematic and minimal

issues.text: Toasts and banners are drawn over the world markers. They are not treated as obstacles, and they sit exactly where the town's markers cluster at the alert camera. In ux-2 the 'Opening West shelter' toast hides a group label. In ux-1 the 'David's Sling deploying' toast sits between the DEPLOY pad and a LOCKED shelter. In ux-3 the 'ALL 92 IN PROTECTED SPACES' banner is crossed by shelter labels (16/24, 8/40) and becomes hard to read. AoE IV and CoH3 never let notification text fight world pins.

At the siren, the things the player must act on are often off-screen or jammed at the screen edge, and nothing points to them. In C2 f00040 the locked Lookout shelter and its 16-person group are wedged into the corner between the clock and the roster, and the second locked shelter (West) is not on screen at all. The roster says LOCKED, but clicking a roster row does not move the camera. The radar shows no shelters or groups. CoH3 and AoE IV use edge arrows and minimap pings for this.

The roster's right column has no right padding: 'LOCKED' and the ETAs (31s, 26s) touch or cross the panel border, and it is worse in compact mode. Feed timestamps are illegible because the row gradient starts fully transparent exactly where <time> sits (23:46 over a road in S2). The barrage subline 'SALVO 2 OF 3 · INTERCEPTS AND FALLING DEBRIS' wraps, leaving 'DEBRIS' as an orphan line in the alert box.

World markers read more like debug tooltips than game pins. Every one is a mono-text box with a 1px stem, and at the S4b wide view or in compact 960x540 the town becomes a field of 14+ boxes with long, crossing leader lines from the 24/48 px lifts. Compact mode zooms the panels to 0.78 but not the markers, so at 960 they dominate (S2-tactical-960). Group feet that drop to 'dot' mode lose all identity. Compare the AoE IV and CoH3 icon-first pins, where text appears on hover or selection.

The pad build popup opens over the air-defence panel and the command bar (ux-0), and marker feet and route rings render under the semi-transparent panels (a group ring under the roster and a diamond between the clock and the roster in C2; the 20/20 pad stem runs into the command bar in S7). The pad label in compact mode shows only '13/20' or 'DEPLOY' with no pad name or battery type.
On the debrief, 'Watch the sky' hides the debrief but leaves .iw-play.dim (opacity 0) on, so the player gets a bare scene with no HUD and no way back to the debrief or to Play again.

The same numbers are framed three ways at once: the roster says 'People outside 92/92', the alert says 'In protected spaces 0/92' and the objective says '0/92'. The debrief says '56/68 threats intercepted' while the AD panel said 86% and the history note says 99%. Each is defensible, but the hierarchy goal is one place per fact.

In compact mode, the AD panel is CSS-zoomed to 0.78, but the radar click handler maps clientX/Y with the unzoomed scale (sc = 226/width), so radar clicks land at the wrong world position below 1100x640.

hud.note: Critic R1: 7/10. Red-alert module near CoH3, start/intro/debrief at AoE IV level; toasts cover markers, no off-screen pointers at the siren, overflows, debug-tooltip markers, small bugs. Round 2 building.
